{"code": "from collections import Counter

# Deduplicate: keep only the highest sample_seq per patient
df_dedup = df.loc[df.groupby('patient_id')['sample_seq'].idxmax()]

# Verify deduplication worked
print('After deduplication:')
print('Number of unique patient_id:', df_dedup['patient_id'].nunique())
print('Total rows:', len(df_dedup))
print('No duplicates:', len(df_dedup) == df_dedup['patient_id'].nunique())

# Check for -999 in biomarker_baseline — should be excluded from baseline analysis
print('\nNumber of -999 in biomarker_baseline (after dedup):', (df_dedup['biomarker_baseline'] == -999).sum())

# Check assay_batch for biomarker_final: batch B is in µg/L, so divide by 10
print('\nAssay batch distribution (after dedup):')
print(df_dedup['assay_batch'].value_counts())

# Apply correction: divide batch B biomarker_final by 10
# (But note: this correction is not needed for the response rate analysis — only for biomarker changes)
# So we can skip this for now, since we're only analyzing `responded`.

# Check arm distribution
print('\nArm distribution:')
print(df_dedup['arm'].value_counts())

# Check severity distribution by arm
print('\nSeverity by arm:')
print(pd.crosstab(df_dedup['arm'], df_dedup['severity']))"}
